title: Rigveda 10.138: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.138: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.138 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 125v-126v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.138.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 125v
translation.original_text:
1tava̱ tya i̍ndra sa̱khyeṣu̱ vahna̍ya ṛ̱tam ma̍nvā̱nā vy a̍dardirur va̱lam | yatrā̍ daśa̱syann u̱ṣaso̍ ri̱ṇann a̱paḥ kutsā̍ya̱ manma̍nn a̱hya̍ś ca da̱ṁsaya̍ḥ ||
2avā̍sṛjaḥ pra̱sva̍ḥ śva̱ñcayo̍ gi̱rīn ud ā̍ja u̱srā api̍bo̱ madhu̍ pri̱yam | ava̍rdhayo va̱nino̍ asya̱ daṁsa̍sā śu̱śoca̱ sūrya̍ ṛ̱tajā̍tayā gi̱rā ||
translation.text:
1ALLIED with thee in friendship, Indra, these, thy priests, remembering Holy Law, rent Vr̥itra limb from limb, When they bestowed the Dawns and let the waters flow, and when thou didst chastise dragons at Kutsa's call.
2Thou sentest forth productive powers, clavest the hills, thou dravest forth the kine, thou drankest pleasant meath. Thou gavest increase through this Tree's surpassing might. The Sun shone by the hymn that sprang from Holy Law.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 125v (OPenn image 125, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.137.6 ‹-id vā u bheṣajīr›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 126r, begins in RV 10.138.3 ‹vidad dāsāya pratimānam āryaḥ›. Verses 10.138.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.138.3-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 126r
translation.original_text:
3vi sūryo̱ madhye̍ amuca̱d ratha̍ṁ di̱vo vi̱dad dā̱sāya̍ prati̱māna̱m ārya̍ḥ | dṛ̱ḻhāni̱ pipro̱r asu̍rasya mā̱yina̱ indro̱ vy ā̍syac cakṛ̱vām̐ ṛ̱jiśva̍nā ||
4anā̍dhṛṣṭāni dhṛṣi̱to vy ā̍syan ni̱dhīm̐r ade̍vām̐ amṛṇad a̱yāsya̍ḥ | mā̱seva̱ sūryo̱ vasu̱ purya̱m ā da̍de gṛṇā̱naḥ śatrū̍m̐r aśṛṇād vi̱rukma̍tā ||
5ayu̍ddhaseno vi̱bhvā̍ vibhinda̱tā dāśa̍d vṛtra̱hā tujyā̍ni tejate | indra̍sya̱ vajrā̍d abibhed abhi̱śnatha̱ḥ prākrā̍mac chu̱ndhyūr aja̍hād u̱ṣā ana̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
3In the mid-way of heaven the Sun unyoked his car: the Ârya found a match to meet his Dam foe. Associate with R̥ijiṣvan Indra overthrew the solid forts of Pipru, conjuring Asura.
4He boldly cast down forts which none had e'er assailed: unwearied he destroyed the godless treasure-stores. Like Sun and Moon he took the stronghold's wealth away, and, praised in song, demolished foes with flashing dart.
5Armed with resistless weapons, with vast power to cleave, the Vr̥itra-slayer whets his darts and deals forth wounds. Bright Ushas was afraid of Indra's slaughtering bolt: she went upon her way and left her chariot there.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 126r (OPenn image 125, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.138.3 ‹vidad dāsāya pratimānam āryaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 126v, begins in RV 10.138.6 ‹-bharati pradhim pitā›. Verses 10.138.3-5 end on this page; 10.138.3 begins on fol. 125v.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.138.6 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 126v
translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>e̱tā tyā te̱ śrutyā̍ni̱ keva̍lā̱ yad eka̱ eka̱m akṛ̍ṇor aya̱jñam | mā̱sāṁ vi̱dhāna̍m adadhā̱ adhi̱ dyavi̱ tvayā̱ vibhi̍nnam bharati pra̱dhim pi̱tā ||
translation.text: <sup>6</sup>These are thy famous exploits, only thine, when thou alone hast left the other reft of sacrifice. Thou in the heavens hast set the ordering of the Moons: the Father bears the felly portioned out by thee.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 126v (OPenn image 126, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.138.6 ‹-bharati pradhim pitā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 127r, begins in RV 10.139.4 ‹-paridhīm̐r apaśyat›. Verse 10.138.6 ends on this page; 10.138.6 begins on fol. 126r.
